turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

That's the interior of bounding box rows1-3 cols1-5 excluding the diagonal lines themselves? Points on diagonals: from (3,0)-(2,1): cell none. From (3,0)-(1,2)? line slope -2.. hmm.

Maybe rule: draw lines between pairs of 3s with same color? Only one color. Lines drawn between 3s along slope ±1 diagonals that exist in input: pairs like (0,3)&(1,2)? slope -1 adjacent diagonal but not same direction. Filled region looks like a diamond interior. Probably: consider all 3s as vertices; fill interior of polygon formed by connecting consecutive vertices? Polygon (0,3)->(1,4)? no (1,4) exists: vertices sorted by row: A(0,3), B(1,2), C(1,4), D(2,1), E(2,5), F(3,0), G(3,6). Convex hull is B-F-G-C-A? Fill convex hull interior minus boundary? Interior of hull includes many more cells though.

Alternatively rule: 2s fill cells lying on straight lines (slope ±1 or axis-aligned?) between pairs of same-color dots. Check: (1,3): between (0,3) vertical and... it's right of (1,2) and left of (1,4) — horizontally between two 3s! (2,3): between (2,1)? and (2,5): horizontal yes. (2,2): between (1,2) and... not horizontal. Between (0,3)? Not aligned. Diagonally between (1,2) and (3,... no 3 at (3,4). Hmm (2,2) lies on diagonal between (0,3) and (3,1)-no 3 there. Between (1,2) and (3,0): midpoint... (2,1)? occupied. So maybe fill convex combinations between every pair of 3s? Line segment between (1,2) and (3,0): passes (2,1) only. Hmm.

Check filled vs pairs: (1,3) horiz between (1,2),(1,4). (2,3) between (2,1),(2,5). (2,2): diag between (0,3)&(3,-1)? no. between (1,2) and (3,0)? no. What about vertical between (0,3)... (3,3) not 3. Hmm (2,2) also between (1,2) & (2,1)? no, those are diagonal neighbors—filling between adjacent diagonals? Actually maybe rule: fill any zero cell that lies on the segment between some pair of colored cells, where "between" uses Chebyshev? (2,2): Chebyshev midpoint of (1,2) and (3,0)? mid=(2,1). Hmm.

Try: cell filled if it's between two 3s along either row, column, or diagonal with both endpoints being 3. For (2,2): anti-diag (i+j=4): 3s at (1,3)? no. diag main (i-j=-0): (1,1)? no. Hmm. Diag with other slope: i+j? (1,2)&? (2,2): j-i=0 diag: cells (0,0)..(3,3): 3s at... none. j+i=4: (0,4)? no. So fails.

Alternative: fill cells enclosed: bounded region whose boundary consists of 3-lines. Region: rows1-3, cols1-5 minus the diagonal edges from (1,2)→? Edges of region: bottom row has 3s at 0..6 spanning 0-6, top edge via (0,3)? The filled shape: (1,3); row2: 2,3,4; row3: 1..5. Top boundary: from (1,2) to (1,4) direct; and (2,1) up-left edge? Left side boundary: cells (2,1)?? not filled. Hmm region: union of triangle tips pointing right/left? Row1: col3 (between 1,2&1,4). Rows2: 2,3,4 (between 2,1&2,5). Row3: 1-5 (between 3,0&3,6). So it's: for each row, fill between the min and max 3 in that row. Row0: single 3 → nothing. Row1: cols2-4 → (1,3). Row2: cols1-5 → 2,3,4. Row3: 0-6 → 1-5. Yes! Rule per-row: fill zeros between min and max colored cell in that row. But then why aren't other cells filled... this matches demo exactly.

But wait, does vertical analog matter? In test we'd do per-column similarly? Test input columns have 6s: col0: rows2; col1: row1; col2: row0; col3: row1; col4: row2; col5: row2; col6: row0; col7: row1; col8: row0. Each column has single or two 6s; filling between min/max per column yields little. Combined result = union over rows+columns? Ambiguous; but simpler: per-row gives reasonable answer. Alternatively fill convex hull-ish union of both directions. Given demo only checks per-row, apply per-row to test: row0: 6s at cols2,8 → fill 3-7. Row1: 6s at 1,3,7 → fill 2,4,5,6. But ambiguity: should we also fill vertically? Column-wise would add e.g. col0: row2 only none; col2: row0 only. Most columns single 6 so nothing extra. Columns with two: col3 only row1; col1 row1; etc. All columns have ≤2 6s, so vertical adds nothing. Union equals just row fills? Wait union doesn't extend beyond anyway. But also need check whether vertical-between-cell pairs (like a 6 above and below) exist — none do. Good. Also what about cells between 6s going down-right diagonals? e.g. (1,2)? not 6. Diagonals: (0,8)&(1,7): (2,6) is 6... cells between (1,7),(2,6): none. (0,2)&(1,3): none between. Fine.

But is union correct, or does order matter? Since no conflicts, submit union. Also maybe rule also requires filling based on "between two of same color" only across rows — same thing here. Submit.
